question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x) = e^{-|2x|}, \quad x \in (-\infty, \infty),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/40ebced9e322ef969e40733356aacdb3971e14276bc6ad54691aeea21b14c488.svg)

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x \leq 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2t}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x > 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/9293ff0dab0e6c12fd143ec5f8a9d72edfce74fcddae2397f19d0e82a8b767cc.svg)
